summary: Retested the iteration_1 fixes on the backend (pytest, 48 tests: 46 pass, 2 fail on precision gaps that were found and documented as known gaps) and on the frontend (Playwright at 375x667, demo flow end to end). Working: matcher rejects all 4 listed false positives and accepts true matches; removing a store deletes that store's deals in the API; deals header total equals the Savings total ($9.04 / $9.04); a live check replaced the sample Target coffee deal with a live Kroger deal; register-push returns 201 {status: skipped}; each demo login creates a separate seeded demo_<hex> user with isolated data; 'On sale' tag stays on one line (17px tall); trash button is 44x44; onboarding edits survive a focus refetch; add/edit/delete, check deals now and exit demo all work. Broken: (a) the Savings tab shows stale data after editing stores, (b) the web focus outline is still visible on the price input, (c) store tiles have no aria-checked on web, (d) snippets are still cut mid-word at the end of the match window, (e) name words are matched as substrings, so 'Eggshell paint' matches unbranded 'Large Eggs'. No deprecated Expo packages detected.

minor.issue: Name and brand words are matched with substring `t in win_low` and the anchor regex has a leading \b only. Unbranded 'Large Eggs' matches 'Eggshell paint $3.49'. Use \b...\b word-boundary regexes. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:368-374

With a brand set, one name word is enough: 'Tyson Chicken Nuggets $7.99' is accepted for 'Tyson Boneless Chicken Breast'. This matches the spec but is a precision gap. Consider requiring all distinctive name words when the item has 2+ of them. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:371-372

The match window is a fixed slice (anchor-25 .. anchor+80), so snippets start and end mid-word. Live example: 'oz 17) Folgers or Café Bustelo Coffee – $9.99 with card Select Varieties, 22-25.9 oz Can, Lim'. Word-boundary trimming only runs when the snippet is over 200 chars. Trim both ends of the window to whitespace. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:369,380-386

Each call creates a new user plus 6 items, 4 deals and 1 alert. Nothing ever removes them and the endpoint has no rate limit, so the database grows without bound, and each demo session can trigger paid Exa searches via /deals/check. Add a TTL index (or periodic cleanup) for is_demo data and a rate limit.

ui_bugs.issue: onboarding save() only invalidates ['deals']. If the Savings tab was already visited, it keeps showing removed-store savings: after removing Target it still showed the $9.04 total and a Target $3.00 row. Add qc.invalidateQueries for 'savings' (and 'alerts'). Reference: /app/frontend/app/onboarding.tsx:52

A black focus rectangle is still drawn when the input is focused. outlineWidth: 0 does not suppress Chrome's 'outline-style: auto' ring (computed 'auto 0px'); use outlineStyle: 'none'. The input also runs past its container (x 62 + width 311 = 373 vs a card edge of about 351), so the ring overflows to the screen edge. Reference: /app/frontend/app/add-item.tsx:117

role='checkbox' renders, but aria-checked is absent on web (accessibilityState is not mapped by react-native-web). Also pass aria-checked={on} (and aria-disabled) through PressScale. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/ui.tsx:35

issues: The in-app alert banner ('Cheerios is BOGO at Walmart') shown right after demo login covers the 'Add an item' title and close button for several seconds
The long name 'Laundry Detergent Pacs' is cut to 'Laundry Deter…' when the On sale tag is shown
The trash button deletes immediately with no confirmation or undo

action_items: onboarding.tsx save(): also invalidate the 'savings' and 'alerts' queries so the Savings tab updates after stores are removed
add-item.tsx priceInput: use outlineStyle: 'none' on web and keep the input inside its container (minWidth: 0 / width constraint)
server.py _windows: use word-boundary regex matching for name and brand terms (fixes 'eggshell' matching 'eggs')
server.py: trim snippet window start and end to word boundaries
Optional: require all distinctive name words even when a brand is present; add TTL cleanup and a rate limit for demo users
PressScale: pass aria-checked / aria-disabled for web accessibility
critical_code_review_comments: The 2 failing tests in test_iteration2_fixes.py::TestMatcherGaps are intentional regression markers for the precision gaps above; they should pass once fixed
On the backend, the live check correctly deletes sample deals only when live deals are found for that item, and keeps previous deals when the Exa search errors
FastAPI on_event is deprecated; move to lifespan handlers (non-blocking)
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_promobeaux_api.py (user_id now asserted as a demo_ prefix; the deals-shape test uses a fresh demo session because the onboarding test now deletes removed-store deals)

success_rate.backend: 96% (46/48; the 2 failures are newly found precision gaps)
success_rate.frontend: ~85% (all flows work; Savings stale after a store edit, price outline still visible, aria-checked missing on web)

seed_data_creation: No manual seeding. Each test or UI run creates throwaway demo_<hex> users via POST /api/auth/demo. TEST_ items were deleted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Demo users are per session (demo_<hex>); do not assume a 'demo_user' id. backend/pytest.ini enables xdist (-n); run with '-n 0' for sequential runs. The live Exa check returns in about 0.5s and found a Kroger Folgers deal. Tab testIDs: tab-deals, tab-watchlist, tab-savings, tab-profile.
rca_of_issue: Stale Savings: tabs stay mounted and react-query only refetches invalidated or remounted queries; onboarding invalidates 'deals' but not 'savings'. Price outline: RN-web sets outline-style:auto on focused inputs, and Chrome draws the auto ring regardless of outline-width:0; outline-style:none is required.
